strings.app.name: Tokendial
strings.panel.noProviders: No providers connected. Right-click for settings.
strings.card.failed: Could not read usage ({why}). Showing nothing rather than a guess.
strings.card.derived: Derived from local activity, not published by the provider
strings.error.keychainRefused: macOS did not allow the keychain read
strings.card.keychainWhy: Tokendial needs it to read the usage this tool already keeps for you: the sign-in is read to call that tool’s own endpoint, never written, and never sent anywhere else. Allow it in Keychain Access, then choose Refresh.
strings.copy.forecastLasts: At this pace it lasts until the reset
strings.alert.threshold.title: {name} at {pct}%
strings.alert.limit.title: {name} limit reached
strings.alert.limit.waiting: Waiting for the window to reset
strings.alert.resetSoon.title: {name} resets soon
strings.alert.resetDone.title: {name} is available again
strings.alert.waiting.title: {name} is waiting for you
strings.alert.waiting.body: An agent is waiting for your input
strings.signin.openApp: Sign in with {name} to read this account.
strings.signin.claude: Run `{command}` once; it signs in and refreshes the token this reads.
strings.signin.grok: Run `grok login`; it signs in and refreshes the token this reads.
strings.signin.opencode: Connect the Go plan inside OpenCode (`opencode auth login`); the dial reads the key it stores.
strings.signin.glm: Usage rides on a Z.ai GLM Coding Plan key held by a coding tool: Claude Code's settings.json, ZCode or OpenCode.
strings.signin.copilot: Sign in to GitHub Copilot in your editor or the Copilot CLI; the dial reads the token it stores.
strings.signin.gemini: Run `gemini` once and choose Login with Google; the dial reads the token it caches. Google serves Gemini CLI only to Code Assist Standard and Enterprise accounts.
strings.settings.title: Tokendial settings
strings.settings.providersHint: Tokendial reads the sign-in each coding tool already keeps on this computer and asks that tool's usage endpoint. Nothing is written back and nothing leaves the machine except that request.
strings.settings.panel.hover: Expand when the cursor reaches the dock
strings.settings.panel.hoverHint: A compact row of dials otherwise.
strings.settings.panel.hiddenHint: Alerts and the tray icon only.
strings.settings.alertsHint: Silent while the panel is expanded under your cursor. At most one alert per provider each minute.
strings.settings.thresholdsFieldHint: For the headline window of each provider.
strings.settings.resetSoonHint: Before a window you have leaned on resets, and once a limit lifts.
strings.settings.waiting: An agent is waiting for you
strings.settings.waitingHint: Repeats every five minutes while it keeps waiting.
strings.settings.delivery.bannersHint: Top-right corner, in your system accent color. Shown even under Do not disturb.
strings.settings.delivery.systemHint: Kept in the notification center; silenced by Do not disturb.
strings.settings.delivery.both: System notifications, banners when the system is silent
strings.welcome.title: Welcome to Tokendial
strings.welcome.intro: A capsule at the top of the screen with one dial per coding assistant, showing how much of each usage limit you have spent, plus a notification when you cross a threshold, when a window is about to reset, when a limit is reached, and when an agent has been waiting on you.
strings.welcome.optIn: Each provider is opt-in. Tokendial reads the sign-in its own tool already stores on this computer and calls that tool's usage endpoint; it never writes credentials and never sends them anywhere else.
strings.welcome.foundHint: Connect the ones you want on the dial.
strings.welcome.nothingHint: Sign in to a supported tool and connect it later from Settings.
strings.welcome.notSignedInHint: Install or sign in from here; Tokendial connects each one as soon as it is signed in.
strings.install.state.notSeen: No sign-in detected yet. Press Sign in once you have finished.
strings.install.sheet.title: Install {name}
strings.install.sheet.intro: Tokendial will open a terminal and run this command from {vendor}:
strings.install.sheet.signInIntro: Tokendial will open a terminal and run {name}'s own sign-in:
strings.install.sheet.uac: Windows may ask for permission while installing.
strings.install.requires.winget: Windows Package Manager (winget) was not found. Install “App Installer” from the Microsoft Store first.
strings.install.requires.brew: Homebrew was not found. Install it from brew.sh first.
strings.install.hint.claude: Claude Code opens in the terminal and sends you to the browser to sign in. Come back once it says you are logged in.
strings.install.hint.codex: Codex opens the browser to sign in with your ChatGPT account.
strings.install.hint.copilot: When Copilot opens in the terminal, type /login and follow the browser steps.
strings.install.hint.grok: Grok opens the browser to sign in with your xAI account.
strings.install.hint.opencode: OpenCode asks which provider to connect: choose OpenCode and follow the sign-in it offers.
strings.install.hint.app: Open {name} and sign in to your account; Tokendial picks it up on its own.
strings.settings.launchAtLoginHint: Start Tokendial in the background when the system boots.
strings.settings.checkForUpdatesHint: Once a day Tokendial asks GitHub Releases whether a newer version exists. Nothing about you is sent; the download waits for you to restart.
strings.settings.license: Free software under the MIT License.
strings.settings.panel.alwaysHint: Stays open with every dial and its detail.
